title: Large Cardinals, Measures, and Elementary Embeddings

items.title: Inaccessible and Mahlo cardinals
items.statement: In ZFC, inaccessible means uncountable regular strong limit: for every cardinal mu<kappa, 2^mu<kappa. Weakly inaccessible means uncountable regular limit. Mahlo means inaccessible with {alpha<kappa: alpha is an uncountable regular cardinal} stationary. Explain equivalence with stationarily many inaccessible cardinals after the strong-limit closure-point argument; this equivalence is proved below, not stipulated. No existence is asserted.

references.title: Monk Chapter 17, weak compactness/Mahlo discussion pp.356–363

items.title: Size and rank bounds below an inaccessible
items.statement: In ZFC, if kappa is inaccessible then |V_alpha|<kappa for alpha<kappa, every x in V_kappa has size <kappa, and every <kappa-sized set of elements of V_kappa belongs to V_kappa. For cardinals mu,nu<kappa, mu^nu<kappa. The strong-limit cardinals below kappa contain a club.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on alpha: the power-set step uses strong limit; at a limit take the supremum of fewer than kappa earlier cardinal bounds and use regularity and infinite cardinal multiplication. For a small subset collect its ranks and bound their supremum below kappa. Bound mu^nu by 2^(mu times nu), handling finite/zero cases. Obtain a club of cardinal strong limits by closure points of the beth operation below kappa, using countable iteration for unboundedness and suprema for closure. AC chooses enumerations and the cardinal bounds.

references.title: Marks Theorem 18.16 p.79, prerequisite size estimate; Monk Chapter 17 pp.356–363

items.title: An inaccessible rank segment models ZFC
items.statement: In ZFC, inaccessible kappa implies (V_kappa,in) satisfies every ZFC axiom. For each cardinal alpha<kappa, inaccessibility of alpha is absolute between V_kappa and V. This does not assert the converse V_kappa models ZFC implies kappa inaccessible.
items.proof_strategy: Check Extensionality and Foundation by transitivity, Infinity by omega in V_kappa, Pairing/Union/Power Set by rank bounds. Separation uses the relativized formula, not ambient truth. Replacement uses ambient Replacement for the internally unique outputs on x, |x|<kappa, and regularity to bound all output ranks. For AC restrict an ambient choice function to a family in V_kappa; its graph has bounded rank. All subsets and functions on ordinals below kappa needed to test cardinalhood, regularity and strong limit have rank below kappa, so these tests agree in both directions.

references.title: Marks Theorem 18.16 p.79; local explicit Choice and inaccessibility-absoluteness clauses

items.title: Complete ultrafilters and measurable cardinals
items.statement: For an infinite cardinal kappa, a filter is kappa-complete if intersections indexed by any ordinal less than kappa stay in the filter; countably complete means omega_1-complete. A measurable cardinal is an uncountable kappa carrying a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter on all subsets of kappa. A normal measure is such a measure for which every regressive f on a measure-one subset of kappa minus {0} is constant on a measure-one subset. Zero-one measure means the indicator of membership in U; distinguish it from real-valued measurability. Definitions and fixed-index intersection tests are choice-free; ambient cardinality language is ZFC.

references.title: Monk Chapter 10; Marks Section 23 pp.93–95

items.title: Measurable cardinals are inaccessible
items.statement: In ZFC, a nonprincipal kappa-complete ultrafilter on uncountable kappa contains no set of size <kappa, and every map into an ordinal below kappa is constant on a measure-one set. Such kappa is inaccessible.
items.proof_strategy: Intersect complements of fewer than kappa singletons; a small-range function with no large fibre gives an empty intersection of fibre complements. A cofinal partition into fewer than kappa bounded sets then contradicts completeness, proving regularity. If an injection e:kappa->P(mu) exists for mu<kappa, let U decide the membership coordinate for every xi<mu. Intersect the chosen coordinate sets; all e(alpha) there are the same, so the intersection has at most one point, contradiction. Thus 2^mu<kappa using AC comparability. Finite/zero-one additivity follows by exclusivity on disjoint unions.

references.title: Marks Section 12 measurable-cardinal discussion; Section 23 Lemma 23.8 p.94

items.title: Set ultraproducts and constant-map ultrapowers
items.statement: For a set-indexed family of nonempty structures in one finite-arity set signature and a proper ultrafilter U on the nonempty index set, quotient the product of carriers by f~g iff {i:f(i)=g(i)} in U. Define constants/functions coordinatewise and relations by U-membership. For a constant family write Ult(M,U) and x maps to [c_x]. Well-definedness is supplied immediately below; AC supplies a nonempty product.

references.title: Marks Definition 13.1 p.56 and Definition 13.4 p.57

items.title: The ultraproduct is a well-defined nonempty structure
items.statement: The equivalence relation, interpreted symbols and constant map in the set ultraproduct are independent of representatives, and the carrier is a nonempty set.
items.proof_strategy: Use reflexivity, symmetry and finite intersections for transitivity of ~. For each finite tuple of changed representatives, intersect their equality sets; interpretations agree there, so upward closure gives identical truth sets modulo U and identical function classes. Replacement/Separation form the quotient and interpreted graphs. AC chooses a product element; constants lie in the product. The constant map is injective since U excludes the empty set.

references.title: Marks Definition 13.1, well-definedness paragraph p.56

items.title: Los theorem for set ultraproducts
items.statement: In ZFC, for every first-order formula phi and product representatives f_1,...,f_n, the ultraproduct satisfies phi([f_1],...,[f_n]) iff {i:M_i satisfies phi(f_1(i),...,f_n(i))} belongs to U. Hence the constant-map embedding into an ultrapower is elementary.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on terms and formulas. Quotient well-definedness handles atoms; ultrafilter dichotomy handles negation; intersections handle conjunction. For existential right-to-left choose a witness in each nonempty coordinate witness set using AC and fill remaining coordinates with a fixed product element. The converse uses a representative of the existing witness. Constant truth sets are either I or empty, establishing elementarity with parameters.

references.title: Marks Theorem 13.2 pp.56–57

items.title: Scott ultrapowers and class-embedding conventions
items.statement: For all set functions f:I->V, use the set of minimum-rank representatives of its U-equivalence class as [f], not the whole proper equivalence class. Put [f] E [g] iff {i:f(i) in g(i)} in U. A definable class embedding means a formula-by-formula elementarity scheme with set parameters; every needed set restriction exists by Replacement. No universe truth predicate, arbitrary class quantification, NBG, or Global Choice is assumed. Converses about a supplied embedding require this definability/set-restriction convention.

references.title: Monk Chapter 17 opening p.341; Marks Definition 23.4 pp.93–94

items.title: Scott coding and set-likeness of ultrapower membership
items.statement: In ZF, Scott representatives exist as nonempty sets, equality and E are well-defined, and each E-predecessor collection is a set.
items.proof_strategy: Bound candidate minimum ranks by rank(f); well-ordering of ordinals gives the least witnessed rank rho, and Separation inside V_(rho+1) forms the Scott class. Two such sets coincide exactly when their functions are U-equivalent. For a predecessor of [g], replace f(i) by empty outside {i:f(i) in g(i)}. The resulting f lies in the set product of g(i) union {empty}. Replacement of this set of functions by their uniquely specified Scott classes yields all predecessors. This does not choose from a proper class and needs no AC.

references.title: Monk Propositions 17.1–17.2 p.341; Marks Definition 23.4 p.93

items.title: Los schema for the universe ultrapower
items.statement: In ZFC the formula-by-formula Los equivalence holds for the Scott ultrapower of V; in particular it is extensional and the constant-map embedding preserves every fixed first-order formula.
items.proof_strategy: Repeat formula induction, explicitly relativizing each fixed formula to the definable Scott domain. At an existential step the coordinate witness collections may be proper classes: first choose the least possible witness rank at each index by Replacement, then use AC on the resulting nonempty SETS of witnesses at those ranks. This is the required repair to an unqualified appeal to AC on classes. Apply the schema to Extensionality. Do not infer a uniform satisfaction predicate for V.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.3 and following extensionality proof pp.341–342

items.title: Countable completeness and transitive collapse
items.statement: In ZFC the Scott ultrapower of V is well-founded iff U is countably complete. If so its extensional setlike membership relation collapses to a transitive definable class M containing all ordinals, with elementary j_U:V->M.
items.proof_strategy: If a nonempty set of classes had no minimal member, DC (from AC) produces a descending sequence; choose representatives from their Scott sets. Intersect the countably many U-large membership sets and obtain a descending membership sequence in V, contradicting Foundation. For the converse choose decreasing U-sets with empty intersection from a failed countable intersection (restrict to the large complement of that intersection); their exit-time function is a nonstandard natural in Ult and subtracting each finite n gives an infinite descending sequence. Apply the published class Mostowski theorem only after set-likeness and extensionality. Elementarity makes j on ordinals increasing; induction gives j(alpha)>=alpha, so the transitive target contains every ordinal.

references.title: Monk pp.341–343; Marks Lemma 23.6 and Exercise 23.7 p.94

items.title: The critical point of a measurable ultrapower
items.statement: For a measure on kappa, j_U(alpha)=alpha for alpha<kappa and kappa<j_U(kappa). Indeed kappa<=[id]_U<j_U(kappa). The embedding fixes V_kappa pointwise.
items.proof_strategy: Induct on alpha<kappa: every predecessor of [c_alpha] has small range after modification, hence a constant U-large fibre. The identity function dominates each constant alpha since bounded subsets are null. For rank fixing use |V_beta|<kappa: an enumeration of each x of size <kappa is fixed on its index, hence j(x)=j``x; induction on rank then fixes x. AC supplies these small enumerations.

references.title: Marks Lemma 23.8 p.94; Monk Chapter 17 critical-point discussion

items.title: Measurability, normal measures and elementary embeddings
items.statement: In ZFC, kappa measurable iff kappa carries a normal measure iff it is the critical point of a definable elementary embedding V->M into a transitive class (with the stated set-restriction convention). For the ultrapower by a measure U on kappa, U is normal iff its collapsed identity class equals kappa.
items.proof_strategy: From an embedding define U_j={X subset kappa:kappa in j(X)} by Separation using the defining parameters. It is proper, nonprincipal and kappa-complete because j fixes every index below kappa. For regressive f, j(f)(kappa)<kappa is fixed; its fibre is large. Thus an arbitrary original measure normalizes via its ultrapower and the seed kappa; never assert the original measure was normal. In a normal ultrapower each ordinal below [id] is represented by a regressive function and hence a constant; conversely [id]=kappa forces any regressive class to be constant. Check diagonal intersections by applying regressiveness to the least failed index, establishing the existing normal-filter convention.

references.title: Marks Exercises 23.9–23.10 pp.94–95; Monk Chapter 17 normalization

items.title: Infinitary syntax and compactness conventions
items.statement: For regular uncountable kappa, L_(kappa,kappa) permits conjunctions/disjunctions and quantifier blocks of length <kappa, with <kappa free variables per formula and finite-arity nonlogical symbols. Formulas are well-founded set syntax trees; satisfaction for a set structure is recursion on these trees. L_(kappa,omega) allows only finite quantifier blocks. Weak compactness for logic restricts the theory and language to size <=kappa; strong compactness allows arbitrary set size. In either case every <kappa-sized subtheory must have a model. No compactness theorem is part of this definition.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.24 pp.358–361 and Chapter 20 infinitary syntax

items.title: Infinitary Los theorem
items.statement: In ZFC, kappa-complete ultrafilters satisfy Los for L_(kappa,kappa) formulas in set ultraproducts, including parameter tuples of length <kappa.
items.proof_strategy: Well-founded induction on syntax. Intersect <kappa equality sets for parameter-representative invariance and <kappa truth sets for conjunctions. If an infinitary disjunction is large then one disjunct is large by completeness and ultrafilter dichotomy. For an existential block, at each coordinate choose one witness tuple from its nonempty set; AC yields the family of tuples, whose columns give product representatives. Conversely extract the coordinate tuple from representatives of the witnessing block. Uniform semantics remains restricted to set structures.

references.title: Monk Theorem 20.1 pp.427–431, extended explicitly to <kappa quantifier blocks

items.title: Weakly compact cardinals
items.statement: In ZFC call kappa weakly compact when it is inaccessible and has the tree property. Prove below equivalence, at inaccessible kappa, with kappa -> (kappa)^2_2 and with <kappa colors. Inaccessibility must not be discarded when mentioning the tree property at successor cardinals.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.23 pp.356–358

items.title: Tree and partition characterizations at an inaccessible
items.statement: For inaccessible kappa, tree property iff kappa -> (kappa)^2_2 iff kappa -> (kappa)^2_mu for every nonzero mu<kappa.
items.proof_strategy: Tree-to-partition: recursively insert each alpha as a new node t_alpha in mu^{<kappa}, following colors c(beta,alpha) along previously occupied nodes until the first new node. There are <kappa previous nodes, so insertion stops; the resulting prefix-closed tree has kappa nodes and levels <kappa by inaccessibility. A cofinal branch contains kappa inserted nodes; one successor color occurs kappa times, giving a homogeneous set. Reverse: extend the tree order to a lexicographic linear order by chosen well-orders of successor cones, with explicit treatment of limit splitting. Color pairs according to agreement of this linear order with a kappa enumeration; a homogeneous set is monotone. At each level <kappa cones force one cone to contain an unbounded monotone tail; those cones form a branch. The precise lexicographic extension lemma still needs a full local verification before readiness.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.23 pp.356–358 and preceding linear-order/tree lemma

items.title: Henkin truth trees for infinitary compactness
items.statement: For inaccessible kappa and a <kappa-satisfiable L_(kappa,kappa) theory T of size <=kappa, construct a kappa-tree of satisfiable partial truth assignments in a fragment of size kappa such that a cofinal branch yields a model of T.
items.proof_strategy: Close the original formulas under subformulas and term substitutions in stages, adjoining fresh witness tuples for existential blocks. Inaccessibility gives kappa^{<kappa}=kappa and regularity keeps each stage small. Each small portion of the expanded theory is satisfiable by recursively interpreting only fresh constants; do not prespecify false values for formulas absent from T. Enumerate the closed fragment with repetitions, and form nodes that are realizable truth assignments to initial segments, constrained only to make encountered axioms true. Levels have at most 2^{|alpha|}<kappa nodes. A branch gives a complete consistent Henkin theory; the term quotient truth induction handles each <kappa conjunction after all its subformulas have appeared below a common stage, and existential blocks by witness constants.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.24 pp.359–361 (correct the printed truth-assignment condition (4))

items.title: Weak compactness and small infinitary theories
items.statement: At inaccessible kappa, weak compactness is equivalent to compactness of L_(kappa,kappa) for theories and signatures of size <=kappa, and also to the corresponding L_(kappa,omega) property.
items.proof_strategy: Tree property gives a branch through the preceding truth tree. Conversely encode a kappa-tree by named nodes, a predicate for each level, the complete atomic diagram and the finite predecessor-comparability axioms, with a new element above a point on each old level. Express each level as the disjunction of its <kappa named nodes. The theory has size kappa, every <kappa part is realized by a sufficiently high node, and a full model gives compatible old predecessors on every level. Only L_(kappa,omega) is used in this direction; do not use the entire infinitary diagram of size kappa^{<kappa} without its cardinal bound.

references.title: Monk Theorem 17.24 pp.358–361

items.title: Regressive injections on nonreflecting sets of cardinals
items.statement: If A is a set of infinite cardinals and A intersect rho is nonstationary in every uncountable regular rho, then A admits an injective regressive map (with any omega endpoint treated explicitly).
items.proof_strategy: Induct on sup(A), splitting successor, singular-limit and regular-limit stages. At a regular limit use a disjoint club and maps on its intervals; at a singular limit choose a continuous cofinal sequence and separate interval ranges while reserving values for endpoints. The endpoint bookkeeping in the source requires checking and a complete correct recursion has not yet been verified. This lemma is a required supplier, not an appeal to an unnamed standard fact.

references.title: Monk Lemma 17.25 p.362

items.title: Weak compactness implies stationary reflection and Mahloness
items.statement: In ZFC, each stationary S subset weakly compact kappa reflects to an uncountable regular rho<kappa. Consequently kappa is Mahlo and has stationarily many inaccessible cardinals below it.
items.proof_strategy: Intersect S with the club of infinite cardinals. If no regular reflection exists, every proper initial segment admits the preceding injective regressive map. The tree of these maps restricted to successively longer initial segments has nonempty levels and level size <kappa by inaccessible cardinal arithmetic. Its branch is a regressive injection on a stationary set, contradicting Fodor. Apply reflection to each club to get a regular point of it, and intersect with the strong-limit closure-point club to get inaccessible points.

references.title: Monk Lemma 17.26 and Theorem 17.27 pp.362–363

items.title: Measurable cardinals are weakly compact
items.statement: In ZFC every measurable cardinal is weakly compact.
items.proof_strategy: Normalize a measure. Given c:[kappa]^2->2, for each alpha select the unique color whose tail fibre is measure-one. One color is selected on a measure-one set. The diagonal intersection of the corresponding tail fibres is measure-one by normality (least failed index would be regressive with a large constant fibre). Intersect with the chosen-color set to obtain a homogeneous set of size kappa. Apply the tree/partition equivalence at the already proved inaccessible cardinal.

references.title: Monk Chapter 10 normal-measure partition proof p.111 and Chapter 17; local two-color specialization

items.title: Fine measures, strong compactness and supercompactness
items.statement: For uncountable regular kappa and cardinal lambda>=kappa, P_kappa(lambda)={x subset lambda:|x|<kappa}. A fine kappa-complete ultrafilter contains {x:alpha in x} for every alpha<lambda. It is normal if f(x) in x on a large set implies f is constant on a large set. Strong compactness means every kappa-complete proper filter on any set extends to a kappa-complete ultrafilter. Lambda-supercompactness means a normal fine kappa-complete ultrafilter on P_kappa(lambda); supercompactness means this for every cardinal lambda>=kappa. No automatic normality for fine measures is assumed.

references.title: Monk Theorem 20.2 p.431 and Lemmas 20.17–20.21 pp.440–442

items.title: Strong compactness, fine measures and infinitary logic
items.statement: For regular uncountable kappa in ZFC: strong compactness iff every P_kappa(lambda), lambda>=kappa, carries a fine kappa-complete ultrafilter iff arbitrary set-sized <kappa-satisfiable L_(kappa,kappa) theories have models iff the same holds for L_(kappa,omega).
items.proof_strategy: Filter extension gives a fine measure by extending the filter generated by cones above <kappa subsets; regularity proves proper kappa-completeness. Fine measures on ordinals transport to P_kappa(T). Choose for each small subtheory a model, using least witness ranks then AC, enlarge to a common signature and take the infinitary ultraproduct. Fineness makes each axiom hold. Conversely introduce unary R_X for all subsets X of the filter index set, one constant d, the complement/intersection identities (including <kappa intersections), nonemptiness and R_X(d) for X in the original filter. Small satisfiability is witnessed by an element in the intersection of the fewer than kappa named filter sets. A full model defines the desired deciding kappa-complete ultrafilter by R_X(d).

references.title: Monk Theorem 20.2 p.431; explicit complement axiom and L_(kappa,kappa) extension

items.title: Fine ultrapower seeds and normality
items.statement: For fine kappa-complete U on P_kappa(lambda), s=[x maps to x]_U contains j``lambda and M thinks |s|<j(kappa). Normality is equivalent to s=j``lambda. In the normal case [x maps to ordertype(x)]_U=lambda and j(kappa)>lambda.
items.proof_strategy: Fineness puts every constant j(alpha) into s. Los gives s in j(P_kappa(lambda)) and the internal size bound. Normality makes each represented member f(x) in x constant on a large set, yielding equality with the seed image. Conversely equality forces such a class to be constant. In the normal case ordertype(s)=lambda by the increasing map j restricted to lambda; apply Los to ordertype to obtain lambda<j(kappa). Keep internal and external cardinal bounds distinct in the merely fine case.

items.title: The covering-embedding characterization of strong compactness
items.statement: In ZFC kappa is strongly compact iff for every cardinal lambda>=kappa there is a definable elementary embedding j:V->M into a transitive class with critical point kappa and some s in M such that j``lambda subset s subset j(lambda) and M satisfies |s|<j(kappa). Retain the set-restriction convention.
items.proof_strategy: Forward take the fine ultrapower. Completeness fixes every ordinal below kappa. Since s contains j``kappa, j(kappa)=kappa would contradict the internal size bound: a size <kappa enumeration of s in M is also an ambient enumeration and cannot cover kappa. Conversely derive U={X subset P_kappa(lambda):s in j(X)}; s belongs to j(P_kappa(lambda)) by the INTERNAL size condition, so U is proper, fine and kappa-complete. Apply the preceding equivalence. For arbitrary lambda the cover need not equal j``lambda and no lambda-sequence closure follows.

references.title: Monk Theorem 20.2 p.431 and covering construction Lemma 20.12 p.438; local seed converse

items.title: Supercompactness and closed elementary embeddings
items.statement: For lambda>=kappa in ZFC, lambda-supercompactness iff there is a definable elementary j:V->M with critical point kappa, j(kappa)>lambda and every ambient lambda-sequence of elements of M in M. Such an embedding yields U={X subset P_kappa(lambda):j``lambda in j(X)}.
items.proof_strategy: Forward: choose representatives f_alpha of a lambda-sequence of M-elements, using Replacement for least possible representative ranks then AC. Put F(x)={f_alpha(x):alpha in x}. Normality and fineness show [F] is exactly the range of the sequence; apply the same construction to ordered pairs (alpha,a_alpha) to recover its graph, hence the sequence is in M. Conversely closure puts the sequence j restricted to lambda, and therefore j``lambda, in M. In M its ordertype is lambda, yielding the internal <j(kappa) size bound. The seed gives a proper kappa-complete fine ultrafilter; regressiveness evaluated at j``lambda gives normality. In both directions completeness fixes ordinals below kappa and the seed bound forces movement at kappa.

items.title: Large-cardinal implication and consistency ledger
items.statement: In ZFC, supercompact -> strongly compact -> measurable -> weakly compact -> Mahlo -> inaccessible. These implications give the corresponding one-way relative consistency implications. Existence of an inaccessible gives a transitive set model of ZFC. No consistency, converse, strictness/equiconsistency, linearity of all large-cardinal notions, or collapse of strong compactness to supercompactness is asserted.
items.proof_strategy: Forget normality for the first arrow; extend the co-small filter on kappa for strong compactness to measurability, checking regularity ensures kappa-completeness and that no singleton can be in its extension. Use earlier local implications for the rest. For relative consistency append the fixed implication proof to any purported weaker-theory refutation to get a stronger-theory refutation; this is an external finite-proof transformation, not an assertion that the theory is consistent. Use set soundness for the rank-model consequence. Report all unresolved supplier holds explicitly.

references.title: Monk Chapters 17 and 20 implication statements; Marks Theorem 18.16

items.title: Laver anticipation functions
items.statement: For supercompact kappa, a Laver function is ell:kappa->V_kappa such that for every set x and every cardinal lambda>=kappa there is a supercompactness embedding j:V->M with j(kappa)>lambda, M^lambda subset M, and j(ell)(kappa)=x. Existence is the following separate theorem, not part of the definition.

references.title: Laver (1978), pp.385–388; full-text source unresolved

items.title: Existence of a Laver function at a supercompact
items.statement: In ZFC every supercompact cardinal has a Laver anticipation function.
items.proof_strategy: Bounded set recursion; explicit closure/measure/evaluation absoluteness; normal fine factor fixes hereditary targets; minimal failure contradiction. Complete local proof with original claim retained.

references.title: Laver (1978), pp.385–388; full text not recovered
Hamkins, A class of strong diamond principles, Theorem 1 pp.7–8; full relevant sketch read

items.title: Generic Boolean filters select ground-model joins
items.statement:
Work in ZF. Let $M$ be a transitive set model of ZF, let $\mathbb B\in M$ be a Boolean algebra which $M$ regards as complete and nontrivial, and let $G\subseteq\mathbb B\setminus\{0\}$ be an externally supplied $M$-generic forcing filter, ordered by the Boolean order. Then $G$ is a proper Boolean ultrafilter. For every $A\in M$ with $A\subseteq\mathbb B$,

$$\bigvee{}^M A\in G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\cap G\ne\varnothing,\qquad \bigwedge{}^M A\in G\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A\subseteq G.$$

The superscript indicates joins and meets computed in $M$. These conclusions apply to ground-model families only; $G$ itself need not be in $M$. No existence of $M$ or $G$, no external completeness of $\mathbb B$, and no form of Choice are assumed.
items.proof_strategy: direct

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, generic-filter definitions pp.2–4; local Boolean dense-set argument

items.title: Boolean truth for a supplied generic extension
items.statement:
Work in ZF. Let $M$ be a transitive set model of ZF, let $\mathbb B\in M$ be internally complete and nontrivial, and let $G\subseteq\mathbb B\setminus\{0\}$ be an externally supplied $M$-generic filter in the Boolean order. Use Boolean names with coefficients in all of $\mathbb B$, including zero, and valuation by $G$. For each fixed finite formula $\varphi$ in the language of membership and every finite tuple of Boolean names $\vec\tau$ in $M$,

$$M[G]\models\varphi(\operatorname{val}_G(\vec\tau))\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \|\varphi(\vec\tau)\|^M\in G.$$

Here $M[G]$ is the set of valuations of Boolean names in $M$, with its actual membership relation, and Boolean values are computed internally in $M$. The assertion does not presume that $M[G]$ satisfies ZF, does not assert existence of $M$ or $G$, and does not give a formal consistency transfer. No form of Choice is used.
items.proof_strategy: direct

references.title: Geschke, Models of Set Theory, Boolean semantics Definition 6.27 pp.26–27; local ground-join truth proof

items.title: ZFC and ordinal preservation for supplied transitive Boolean generic extensions
items.statement:
Assume ZFC. Let $M$ be a transitive set model of ZFC, let $\mathbb B\in M$ be internally complete and nontrivial, and supply an $M$-generic filter $G$ on $\mathbb B\setminus\{0\}$. Then the set structure $M[G]$ satisfies ZFC and has exactly the ordinals of $M$. Separation and Replacement are asserted formula by formula. Choice in $M$ is used to select a set of existential witness names and to well-order ground sets of subnames.

The assertion is conditional on the supplied transitive model and generic. It does not assert their existence, a forcing theorem for arbitrary possibly ill-founded models, or a formal consistency implication.
items.proof_strategy: direct

references.title: Karagila, Forcing, section 2 generic extensions; local explicit name proof of axiom preservation

items.title: Supercompact preparation interface
items.statement: Binding preparation target: from a ZFC ground model with a supercompact kappa, obtain a forcing extension in which kappa remains supercompact and its supercompactness is indestructible by further <kappa-directed-closed set forcing. Separate a semantic ground-model construction from any formal Con transfer.
items.proof_strategy: UNRESOLVED: needs the Laver iteration, its support convention, factorization j(P)=P*Q*tail, master condition, tail closure and generic construction, and an embedding-lifting theorem. These are not supplied by SET-23 current roots or by the anticipation theorem alone. Exact proposed placement and unchanged downstream target are in batch notes; declared deps here are only the existing local inputs, not a complete dependency claim.

references.title: Laver (1978), pp.385–388; SET-23 and SET-27 design interface

items.title: Fine-measure coordinates avoiding small supports
items.statement:
In ZFC let $\kappa$ be strongly compact and $\lambda\ge\kappa$ a cardinal. There exist a set $I$, a nonprincipal $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter $U$ on $I$, and functions $f_\alpha:I\to\kappa$ for $\alpha<\lambda$ such that

$$\{x:f_\alpha(x)<f_\beta(x)\}\in U\quad(\alpha<\beta<\lambda),\qquad \{x:f_\alpha(x)>\delta\}\in U\quad(\alpha<\lambda,\ \delta<\kappa).$$

Consequently, for every finite $F\subseteq\lambda$ and every $S\subseteq\kappa$ with $|S|<\kappa$, the following set belongs to $U$:

$$H(F,S)=\{x\in I:f_\alpha(x)\ne f_\beta(x)\text{ for distinct }\alpha,\beta\in F,\ \text{and }f_\alpha(x)\notin S\text{ for all }\alpha\in F\}.$$

The construction takes $I=P_\kappa(\rho)$ for a cardinal $\rho>\kappa+\lambda$, with ordinal addition in this bound. It does not require normality of $U$ or a cofinality restriction on $\lambda$.
items.proof_strategy: Use a fine ultrafilter on a Hartogs-sized index. Define coordinates as order types of initial segments; point cones give comparison, small intersections of cones give domination of every constant, and completeness gives simultaneous avoidance.

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva (2023), Lemma 2.8 pp.6–7 and Theorem 2.10 pp.9–10; strong-compactness specialization

items.title: Probability algebras, arbitrary joins and the countable chain condition
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a probability space, so $\mu(X)=1$. Identify $A,B\in\Sigma$ when $\mu(A\mathbin{\triangle}B)=0$, and write $\mathbb B$ for the set of equivalence classes. Set operations induce Boolean operations on $\mathbb B$, and $m([A])=\mu(A)$ is a well-defined strictly positive probability on it. The order is $[A]\le[B]$ exactly when $\mu(A\setminus B)=0$.

The Boolean algebra $\mathbb B$ is complete. Every subset $D\subseteq\mathbb B$ has a countable subset $D_0\subseteq D$ with $\bigvee D=\bigvee D_0$, allowing $D_0=\varnothing$. Every antichain of nonzero elements is countable. For arbitrary $D\subseteq\mathbb B$ and $c\in\mathbb B$,

$$c\wedge\bigvee D=\bigvee\{c\wedge d:d\in D\}.$$

Countable joins are represented by countable unions of measurable representatives. No assertion that an arbitrary union of representatives is measurable or represents its Boolean join is made.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Solovay densities and localized small null joins
items.statement:
Assume ZFC. Let $\kappa$ be an uncountable cardinal with $|[0,1]|<\kappa$, let $U$ be a proper $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter on a set $I$, and let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a probability space with probability algebra $(\mathbb B,m)$. For every $a=(a_i)_{i\in I}\in\mathbb B^I$ there is a unique almost-everywhere class of measurable functions $h_a:X\to[0,1]$ such that, for every $c\in\mathbb B$,

$$\int_c h_a\,d\mu=\nu_a(c),\qquad \{i:m(c\wedge a_i)=\nu_a(c)\}\in U.$$

Here $\int_c$ means integration over any measurable representative of $c$. This class assignment is a set function on $\mathbb B^I$. The following identities are independent of the chosen representatives of the densities:

1. If $c\wedge a_i=c\wedge b_i$ for all $i$ in some member of $U$, then $h_a=h_b$ almost everywhere on $c$.
2. If $Z\subseteq I$ and $a_i=1$ on $Z$, $a_i=0$ off $Z$, then $h_a$ is the constant $1$ when $Z\in U$ and the constant $0$ otherwise. Coordinatewise complementation gives $h_{\neg a}=1-h_a$ almost everywhere.
3. For a sequence $(a^n)_{n<\omega}$ in $\mathbb B^I$, let $a_i=\bigvee_n a_i^n$. If $c\wedge a_i^n\wedge a_i^r=0$ for every $i\in I$ and $n\ne r$, then $h_a=\sum_n h_{a^n}$ almost everywhere on $c$. The sum is finite almost everywhere on $c$.
4. For any ordinal $\beta<\kappa$ and family $(a^\xi)_{\xi<\beta}$ in $\mathbb B^I$, set $a_i=\bigvee_{\xi<\beta}a_i^\xi$. If every $h_{a^\xi}$ is zero almost everywhere on the same $c$, then $h_a$ is zero almost everywhere on $c$.

In particular, writing $z(a)=[\{x:h_a(x)=0\}]\in\mathbb B$, the last assertion is the Boolean inequality

$$\bigwedge_{\xi<\beta}z(a^\xi)\le z(a).$$

This is a theorem inside the original probability space and its algebra. It does not assert a forcing truth lemma or the existence of a measure on new subsets in a generic extension.
items.proof_strategy: direct

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva (2023), Theorem 2.9 p.8; local proof of the ground probability-algebra density construction and identities

items.title: Generic evaluation of bounded measurable functions by rational cuts
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $M$ be a transitive set model of ZFC containing a probability space $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$, let $\mathbb B$ be its probability algebra computed in $M$, and let $G\subseteq\mathbb B\setminus\{0\}$ be an externally supplied $M$-generic filter. All measurable functions, sequences, null equalities and algebra operations below are ground-model objects computed in $M$. Represent real numbers as lower Dedekind cuts. For a bounded nonnegative measurable function $h$, define the rational set

$$h_G=\{q\in\mathbb Q:[\{x:h(x)>q\}]\in G\}.$$

This is a nonnegative real cut and is the valuation of a Boolean name in $M$, hence belongs to $M[G]$. It depends only on the almost-everywhere class of $h$. Constants evaluate to the same real, and evaluation preserves addition of bounded nonnegative functions. If $c\in G$ and $h\le k$ almost everywhere on a measurable representative of $c$, then $h_G\le k_G$; equality on $c$ gives equality of evaluations. For bounded nonnegative $h$,

$$h_G=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad [\{h=0\}]\in G.$$

If a ground sequence of bounded nonnegative measurable functions $(h_n)$ and a bounded nonnegative measurable $h$ satisfy $h=\sum_{n<\omega}h_n$ almost everywhere on $c\in G$, then $h_G=\sum_{n<\omega}(h_n)_G$. Empty sums evaluate to zero. The conclusions concern this explicitly supplied generic and ground sequences; ZFC preservation and generic existence are not asserted.
items.proof_strategy: direct

references.title: Bagaria and da Silva, section 2.2 Theorem 2.9 p.8, density interpretation sketch; local rational-cut construction

items.title: Solovay measure on all ground-set subsets in a supplied generic extension
items.statement:
Assume ZFC. Let $M$ be a transitive set model of ZFC in which $\kappa$ is an uncountable cardinal, $|[0,1]|<\kappa$, $U$ is a proper $\kappa$-complete ultrafilter on a set $I$, and $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ is a probability space with probability algebra $\mathbb B$. All these parameters and their indicated properties are computed in $M$. Supply an $M$-generic filter $G$ on the nonzero elements of $\mathbb B$. Put $\mathcal D=\{A\in M[G]:A\subseteq I\}$, with actual subset inclusion.

There exist $\mathcal D,\eta\in M[G]$ such that $\eta$ is a function on exactly $\mathcal D$, with values real lower cuts in $[0,1]$, $\eta(I)=1$, and $\eta(\varnothing)=0$. It extends the ground ultrafilter measure: for $Z\in M$ with $Z\subseteq I$, $\eta(Z)=1$ if $Z\in U$ and $0$ otherwise. Every disjoint sequence $(A_n)_{n<\omega}$ belonging to $M[G]$, with all $A_n\in\mathcal D$, has its union in $\mathcal D$ and satisfies

$$\eta\left(\bigcup_{n<\omega}A_n\right)=\sum_{n<\omega}\eta(A_n).$$

For every ground ordinal $\beta<\kappa$ and every family $(A_\xi)_{\xi<\beta}\in M[G]$ in $\mathcal D$, if $\eta(A_\xi)=0$ for all $\xi<\beta$, then its union belongs to $\mathcal D$ and has measure zero. These are assertions for all subsets and indexed families present in this supplied extension, not only ground subsets or ground families. They do not assert that arbitrary external subsets or sequences belong to $M[G]$, that $\kappa$ is preserved, that the extension satisfies ZFC, or a formal consistency implication.
items.proof_strategy: direct

items.title: Strong compactness and the product-measure extension interface
items.statement: Binding product-measure target: Con(ZFC + a strongly compact cardinal) implies Con(ZFC + PMEA), where for every cardinal lambda the standard fair-coin product measure on {0,1}^lambda extends to a countably additive measure on its full power set whose null ideal is closed under unions of fewer than continuum many sets. This is a relative-consistency interface, not a ground-model implication and not a zero-one measure on the index cardinal.
